opts: Effacement with slow dilatation; then rapid dilatation with descent
Descent with slow dilatation; then effacement with no further change
Rapid dilatation with descent; then effacement with slow progress
Effacement only, no dilatation; then descent with slow cervical change
exp: The latent phase is the event of effacement with slow dilatation; the active phase is rapid dilatation with partial descent of the fetal head.

opts: Foley through the cervix, bulb inflated, saline infused extra-amniotically
Saline infused into the amniotic cavity through an amniocentesis needle
Saline infused into the bladder to compress the lower uterine segment
Intravenous saline with oxytocin running through the same catheter
exp: EASI places a Foley in the endocervical canal, inflates the bulb and infuses normal saline at 30-40 ml/hr; the saline collects in the extra-amniotic space, separates the membranes and releases prostaglandins.

opts: Bile acids act only on maternal skin and cause itching, with no fetal effect
Bile acids reduce amniotic fluid production to zero and arrest fetal gut motility
Swallowed bile-salt-rich fluid irritates the fetal bowel and triggers meconium passage
Bile acids paralyse fetal bowel activity so that no meconium is passed at all
exp: Bile salts in the amniotic fluid are swallowed by the fetus, irritate the bowel and trigger meconium passage, which underlies meconium-stained liquor and aspiration syndrome in ICP.

opts: Emergency C-section facility, senior supervision, baby under 4 kg, IV fluids, CTG
Emergency C-section facility, senior supervision, baby up to 4.5 kg, oral fluids
Emergency C-section facility, registrar alone, baby under 4 kg, intermittent CTG
Emergency C-section facility, senior supervision, baby under 4 kg, no CTG needed
exp: Assisted breech delivery requires a centre with emergency C-section facilities, senior supervision, an estimated fetal weight under 4 kg, nil by mouth with IV fluids, and continuous CTG monitoring.

opts: Neuroprotective action (prevents cerebral palsy); given when PTL is under 32 weeks
Tocolytic action (arrests uterine contractions); given when PTL is under 32 weeks
Neuroprotective action (prevents cerebral palsy); given when PTL is over 34 weeks
Tocolytic action (arrests uterine contractions); given when PTL is over 34 weeks
exp: MgSO4 in preterm labour is given for its neuroprotective action (reducing cerebral palsy), and it is given in all cases of PTL before 32 weeks.

opts: Vaginal delivery; C-section at 4.5 kg in diabetics or 5.0 kg in non-diabetics
Vaginal delivery; C-section at 4.0 kg in diabetics or 4.5 kg in non-diabetics
Elective C-section for all; no weight threshold is applied in either group
Vaginal delivery only; C-section at 4.5 kg in diabetics and non-diabetics alike
exp: In macrosomia vaginal delivery is the usual mode; caesarean is advised at 4.5 kg in diabetics and at 5.0 kg in non-diabetics.

opts: Under half the external sphincter : over half the external sphincter : both sphincters
Over half the external sphincter : under half the external sphincter : internal sphincter
Internal sphincter alone : external sphincter alone : rectal mucosa additionally
External sphincter partial : rectal mucosa involved : internal sphincter alone
exp: Third-degree tears are subclassified as 3A (under 50% of external anal sphincter), 3B (over 50% of EAS) and 3C (internal and external anal sphincter).

opts: One mature ovum and three non-functional polar bodies
Four mature ova, all of them fertilisable
Sixteen mature ova, all of them fertilisable
Sixty-four mature ova, all of them fertilisable
exp: Unlike spermatogenesis, where one spermatogonium yields 64 spermatids, each oogonium ultimately gives rise to a single mature ovum (female pronucleus) plus non-functional polar bodies.

opts: High placental oestrogen and progesterone block prolactin at the breast receptors
Low oxytocin from the posterior pituitary fails to trigger milk ejection
High maternal thyroid hormone inhibits milk synthesis within the alveoli
Prolactin secreted in pregnancy is biologically inactive at the receptor
exp: Lactation is held in check during pregnancy by high circulating placental estrogen and progesterone, which competitively block prolactin action at the breast alveolar receptors; delivery lifts the block and unleashes lactation.

opts: Blood from a vessel clots, whereas pouch-of-Douglas blood does not clot
Blood from a vessel does not clot, whereas pouch-of-Douglas blood clots
Both samples clot identically, so clotting cannot distinguish them
Neither sample ever clots, since both are defibrinated on aspiration
exp: Aspirate drawn from a blood vessel clots, whereas blood from the pouch of Douglas in hemoperitoneum has lost clotting factors and does not clot.

opts: Groove; tonically contracted upper segment; passively distended lower segment
Groove; passively distended upper segment; tonically contracted lower segment
Bulge; relaxed and atonic upper segment; tonically contracted lower segment
Ridge; tonically contracted upper segment; hypertonic non-distended lower
exp: Bandl's ring is the groove between the retracted (tonically contracted) upper segment and the distended (passively dilated) lower segment.

opts: 20-24 weeks, from progesterone- and nitric oxide-mediated vasodilatation
6 weeks in the first trimester, from maternal dehydration and hypovolaemia
38 weeks in the third trimester, from placental ischaemia and vasospasm
Blood pressure never falls, as cardiac output matches vascular resistance
exp: Maternal systemic blood pressure reaches its nadir in the mid-second trimester (20-24 weeks), driven by progesterone- and nitric oxide-mediated systemic vasodilatation that lowers peripheral vascular resistance.

opts: Compensated respiratory alkalosis: pCO2 28-32, HCO3 18-22, pH 7.40-7.45
Uncompensated metabolic acidosis: pCO2 45-50, HCO3 12-16, pH 7.20-7.28
Acute respiratory acidosis: pCO2 55-60, HCO3 26-30, pH 7.22-7.30
Metabolic alkalosis with hypokalaemia: pCO2 45-50, HCO3 32-36, pH 7.50-7.55
exp: Normal pregnancy shows a chronic compensated respiratory alkalosis, with pCO2 28-32 mmHg, HCO3 18-22 mEq/L and arterial pH held at 7.40-7.45.

opts: Fully dilated os; Occiput/favourable position; Rotated head and Ruptured membranes; Consent and Contractions; Episiotomy, Engaged, Empty bladder; Pelvis adequate; CPD absent
Forceps blades ready; Obstetrician experienced; Room prepared; Consent obtained; Epidural sited; Pelvis assessed; Scissors available
Full term gestation; Occiput anterior; Rupture the membranes; Catheterise the bladder; Episiotomy cut; Push with pains; Stitch the perineum
Fetal heart checked; Oxygen running; Rotate the head fully; Cut an episiotomy; Extract the head; Pull steadily; Suture the tear afterwards
exp: FORCEPS expands as: Fully dilated os; Occiput/favourable position; Rotated head + Ruptured membranes; Consent + Contracting uterus; Episiotomy + Engaged head + Empty bladder; Pelvis adequate; CPD absent.

opts: Long, the only forceps that can rotate the head, with a sliding lock; outdated
Short outlet forceps with a fixed English lock and no rotation; still used
Longest forceps designed for the aftercoming head in breech; still used
Solid-bladed forceps with a fixed English lock and no rotation; outdated
exp: Kielland forceps are long, are the only forceps that can rotate the fetal head (rotation forceps), have a sliding lock, and are now largely outdated.

opts: TTTS from deep vascular anastomoses; cord entanglement
Cord entanglement; TTTS from deep vascular anastomoses
Vanishing twin in one sac; TRAP sequence in the other
Selective IUGR from unequal placental sharing; TAPS in both
exp: MCDA twins specifically risk TTTS through deep vascular connections; MCMA twins specifically risk cord entanglement.

opts: It creates a gradient that drives CO2 rapidly from fetal blood into maternal blood
It stimulates fetal renal surfactant synthesis and accelerates lung maturity
It prevents premature rupture of membranes by lowering amniotic fluid pressure
It inhibits fetal cardiac output so that placental flow is preferentially raised
exp: Maternal physiological respiratory alkalosis (pCO2 28-32 mmHg) establishes a favourable partial pressure gradient promoting rapid transfer of CO2 from fetal circulation to maternal blood.

opts: Wait for separation signs, push the uterus up, then pull the cord forward during a contraction
Pull on the cord continuously from delivery, regardless of any signs of separation
Squeeze the fundus (Credé manoeuvre) while pulling the cord downwards firmly
Apply traction between contractions while an assistant presses on the fundus
exp: Controlled cord traction: look for signs of separation, push the uterus upwards with one hand, then apply gentle downward-forward traction on the cord during a contraction.

opts: Prematurity, since spontaneous rotation has not yet occurred; uterine malformation
Uterine malformation; prematurity, since spontaneous rotation has not yet occurred
Placenta previa preventing engagement; uterine fibroids distorting the cavity
Oligohydramnios limiting movement; multiple pregnancy crowding the cavity
exp: The commonest cause of breech overall is prematurity (spontaneous rotation has not yet occurred) and of recurrent breech is uterine malformation.

opts: Both ischial spines can be touched at once with the fingers of one hand
Neither ischial spine can be reached at all on vaginal examination
The sacral promontory is easily reached and projects prominently forward
The subpubic arch is unusually wide and the side walls are divergent
exp: The bedside clue to a contracted mid-pelvis is being able to touch both ischial spines simultaneously with the fingers of the same hand.

opts: Pass urine and take oral fluids within 2 hours; watch for PPH, tears, hematoma
Remain nil by mouth for a full 6 hours; watch for uterine rupture
Strict bed rest for 24 hours after delivery; watch for deep vein thrombosis
Keep the catheter in place for 12 hours; watch for postpartum infection
exp: In the fourth stage the mother is advised to pass urine and take oral intake within 2 hours of delivery; the complications to watch for are PPH, perineal tears and vulval hematoma.

opts: Height less than period of gestation, fundus and pelvis empty; cord prolapse risk highest
Height more than period of gestation, head in the fundus; shoulder dystocia likely
Height equal to period of gestation, head in the pelvis; postpartum haemorrhage
Buttocks felt in the fundus, head ballotable above; face presentation likely
exp: In transverse lie the uterine height is less than the period of gestation and both the fundal and deep pelvic grips are empty; it carries the highest risk of cord prolapse because the cervix is not closed by the head.

opts: Below 11.0 g/dL in the first and third trimesters, below 10.5 g/dL in the second
Below 12.0 g/dL in the first and third trimesters, below 11.0 g/dL in the second
Below 10.0 g/dL in the first and third trimesters, below 9.0 g/dL in the second
Below 11.0 g/dL in the second trimester, below 10.5 g/dL in the first and third
exp: Under WHO and CDC definitions anemia in pregnancy is hemoglobin below 11.0 g/dL in the first and third trimesters, or below 10.5 g/dL in the second (reflecting mid-trimester hemodilution).

opts: 400 micrograms daily started at 20 weeks and continued until delivery
No folic acid is advised, since diet alone supplies enough in diabetic pregnancy
400 micrograms daily from 1 month before conception to 3 months after
5 mg daily given only during labour and the immediate postpartum period
exp: For prevention of diabetic congenital anomalies the listed schedule is 400 micrograms of folic acid daily, from 1 month before conception through 3 months after conception.

opts: Hydroxyprogesterone IM weekly from 16-20 weeks to 36 weeks; micronised PV daily
Hydroxyprogesterone IM weekly from 16-20 weeks to 36 weeks; micronised PV weekly
Hydroxyprogesterone orally daily until 20 weeks; micronised IM at 36 weeks
Hydroxyprogesterone as a single IM dose at 12 weeks; no further doses after
exp: The listed progesterone regimens are hydroxyprogesterone caproate IM weekly starting at 16-20 weeks and stopping at 36 weeks, and micronised progesterone per vaginam daily.

opts: After crowning; when the perineum climbs in breech; before traction with forceps
Before crowning; when the perineum climbs in breech; before traction with forceps
After crowning; at full dilatation regardless of descent; before forceps application
After crowning; when the perineum climbs in breech; after delivery of the head
exp: Episiotomy is correctly timed after crowning, when the perineum climbs in breech delivery, and before or after forceps application but always before traction.

opts: Mechanical cervical ripening followed by oxytocin; prostaglandins avoided
Misoprostol 25 micrograms vaginally for ripening; oxytocin is avoided
Dinoprostone gel for cervical ripening; mechanical methods are avoided
Induction is never attempted, so elective caesarean is always performed
exp: Induction of labour in a previous C-section is done by a mechanical method for cervical ripening followed by oxytocin; prostaglandins are avoided.
